case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment caption.

accused_gender.reason: Accused is referred to as male throughout.

accused_age.reason: No age for the accused appears; only that he joined the army in 1983.

accused_religion.reason: Religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: Caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_occupation.reason: Judgment describes the accused as an army official (Ex-Signalman, Lance Naik).

victim_gender.reason: Deceased is referred to as male (Havildar R.C. Tiwari).

victim_age.reason: The deceased's age is not stated anywhere in the judgment.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Judgment states the deceased was a colleague of the accused.

offence_category.reason: Offence is murder under s.302 IPC read with s.69 Army Act.

statutory_provisions.quote: Section 302 read with Section 69 of the Army Act
statutory_provisions.reason: Matches the charged provisions; s.304 Part II and s.300 Exception I are also discussed.

weapon.reason: Weapon identified as a kitchen knife, described as sharp-edged.

evidence_type.quote: PW-1 Paulose who is the eyewitness and PW-3 ... dying declaration
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness, dying declaration, and medical (PW-9) evidence are all relied on.

confession.reason: No confession is mentioned in the judgment.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: due deliberation on the part of the appellant
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Court relies on deliberation, sharp weapon, and vital body part.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating circumstance is recognised; provocation was rejected.

trial_court_outcome.quote: sentenced him to undergo 7 years of rigorous imprisonment and he was also dismissed from service
trial_court_outcome.reason: Matches the General Court Martial finding of guilt and original sentence.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: Writ petition dismissed; conviction and life sentence upheld
high_court_outcome.quote: the Writ Petition was dismissed vide judgment dated 25.8.2005
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court dismissed the writ petition; it did not itself confirm the conviction and sentence.

final_outcome.quote: the appeal has no merit and, accordingly, it is dismissed
final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, upholding the conviction.

offence_finally_established.quote: conviction of the appellant for the offence under Section 302 of Indian Penal Code, is not bad in law
offence_finally_established.reason: Offence established is murder under s.302 IPC.

imprisonment_type.quote: sentenced the appellant to imprisonment for life and dismissal from service
imprisonment_type.reason: Life imprisonment was the sentence imposed on revision.

imprisonment_years.reason: Life imprisonment has no fixed term, so null is appropriate.

fine_rs.reason: No fine is stated in the final sentence; only life imprisonment and dismissal.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Facts of the incident, complaint, weapon, and sentence history without the High Court's reasoning on the outcome.
neutral_facts.quote: The High Court rejected these arguments, finding that the accused had sufficient time to deliberate and plan the attack
neutral_facts.reason: Facts are accurate, but stating the High Court's rejection and reasoning reveals the court outcome.

offence_severity.correct_value: Life imprisonment and dismissal from service
offence_severity.quote: he could be either sentenced to life imprisonment or death sentence
offence_severity.reason: Death was only an option considered; the imposed severity was life imprisonment and dismissal.

attempt_completion.reason: Offence completed as the deceased died from the stab injury.

physical_harm.quote: stabbed the deceased on the right side of the chest
physical_harm.reason: Death from a single stab injury to the chest is supported.

number_of_offences.quote: Charges were framed against the appellant under Section 302 read with Section 69
number_of_offences.reason: A single charge of murder was framed and upheld.

financial_property_loss.reason: Judgment does not address property or financial loss; 'Not applicable' asserts more than the text says.

premeditation_planning.quote: The appellant clearly had time to deliberate and plan out the death
premeditation_planning.reason: Court found time to deliberate and plan, supporting premeditation.

motive.quote: to avenge his humiliation at the hands of the appellant
motive.reason: Motive of avenging humiliation is stated (judgment text has 'appellant' where 'deceased' is meant).

key_evidence_accepted.quote: From the evidence on record, it is very clear that the appellant intended to cause death.
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court's acceptance of evidence on intention and the weapon/body-part reasoning is supported.

witness_credibility.quote: the testimony of PW-1 Paulose who is the eyewitness and PW-3 Haveldar lndrpal ... is reliable
witness_credibility.reason: High Court found both eyewitness and dying-declaration witness reliable.

trial_duration.quote: by an order dated 15.1.1999, revised the sentence
trial_duration.reason: Trial judgment date 25.08.2005 is the High Court date; the court martial order was 15.1.1999.

legal_representation.quote: K.K. Mani, Ankit Swarup and K, Lakshminarayan for the Appellant
legal_representation.reason: Counsel names for both sides match the judgment.

investigation_status.quote: An FIR was lodged at the Dehu Road Police Station vide CR-26 of 1998
investigation_status.reason: FIR, investigation, and charge-sheet are described; trial was completed via court martial.

procedural_irregularity.quote: the procedure under Army Act followed without any infringement of principles of natural justice
procedural_irregularity.reason: High Court found no procedural irregularity; the vagueness challenge was rejected.

appeal_history.quote: The appellant being aggrieved by the same filed a writ petition before the Bombay High Court
appeal_history.reason: Trial, High Court writ, and Supreme Court appeal outcomes match the judgment.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Union of India argued findings and punishment upheld, facts proved s.302 offence, and judicial review was limited.
prosecution_argument.quote: the facts and evidence on record are enough to prove that the offence committed by the appellant falls under Section 302
prosecution_argument.reason: Main thrust matches, but planning and weapon reasoning are the court's own analysis, not counsel's stated argument.

defence_argument.quote: the death of the deceased was caused due to grave and sudden provocation
defence_argument.reason: Provocation under Exception I and s.304 Part II arguments are accurately stated.

legal_principle_applied.quote: It is the nature of injury, the part of body where it is caused, the weapon used ... are the indicators of the fact
legal_principle_applied.reason: Intention as key factor, with injury, body part, and weapon as indicators, is supported.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Mancini v. Director of Public Prosecution (1942) A.C. 200; Rex v. Lesbini (1914) 3 K.B.1116; Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1958 SC 465
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Relied-upon authorities are accurately listed; distinguished cases are omitted, which is acceptable.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: Court upheld s.302 conviction because intention to cause death was proved and s.304 Part II and Exception I were not attracted; sentencing reasoning not separately discussed.
sentencing_rationale.quote: In light of this finding, the evidence on record makes it clear that Section 304 (Part-II) IPC will not be attracted.
sentencing_rationale.reason: Court addressed conviction and intention, not sentencing; the life-sentence rationale is inferred.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: No mitigating factors were recognised by the court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Court relied on deliberation, sharp kitchen knife, and blow to vital part of chest to establish intention (not expressly as sentencing aggravators).
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: The nature of weapon used and the part of the body where the blow was struck, which was a vital part of the body
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court did rely on these factors, so 'None' understates them, though not framed as sentencing aggravators.

other_sentence_order.reason: Only life imprisonment and dismissal from service were ordered; no other order is stated.
